title: RunReport
description: What `cargo xtask evidence run` writes to `report.json` after a run.

commandExitCode.description: The exit code of the command, or null when a signal killed it.

commandSignal.description: The signal that killed the command, or null.

interrupted.description: True when the wrapper received SIGINT or SIGTERM.

problems.description: Every problem that fails the run.

records.description:
Every record, each with its own `context`, so a reader can take one
record without its report.

BaselineMatch.description: How a run's host compares with the recorded baseline host.

matches.description:
True when model, chip, memory, core counts, and `virtualized` are all
present and equal.

osBuildMatches.description:
True when the macOS build also matches, tracked apart because it
changes more often than the hardware.

EvidenceRecord.description:
One evidence record: one test function in one run, or one manual review.

The Rust types are the source of truth; `cargo xtask codegen` publishes
the JSON Schema to `schemas/evidence/`. Unknown fields are accepted, so
`v1` can grow with optional fields.

actual.description: What was observed. Required for `PASS` and `FAIL`.

context.description:
The run context; present in `report.json` and manual records, absent
from raw record files.

covers.description: The PRD IDs this test proves.

evidencePath.description:
Automated: `output.log` or `artifacts/<id>/`, relative to the run
folder. Manual: a path relative to the repository.

expected.description: The expected behavior in one sentence.

finishedAt.description: When the final result was written; null while `NOT_RUN`.

id.description: A UUID v7, also the name of the raw record file.

kind.description: Fixture or native; equal to the kind of the run.

reviewer.description: The reviewer of a manual record.

startedAt.description: When the guard or trait was created, or the manual record written.

steps.description: Manual steps; always null for an automated record.

subjects.description: The providers or runtimes the test ran against.

Host.description:
The machine a run or a baseline was recorded on.

Holds no host name and no user name.

efficiencyCores.description: `sysctl -n hw.perflevel1.physicalcpu`, null when the key is missing.

performanceCores.description: `sysctl -n hw.perflevel0.physicalcpu`, null when the key is missing.

virtualized.description: True when `sysctl -n kern.hv_vmm_present` is 1, null outside macOS.

Kind.description:
Whether a test needs only fakes and fixtures, or a real provider runtime
or something only a macOS 27 Mac has.

oneOf.description: Fakes, mocks, dummy servers, fake providers, or contract fixtures.
A real provider binary, or something only a macOS 27 Mac has.

Language.description: The language a test is written in, or `manual` for a review.

oneOf.description: A Rust `#[test]`.
A Swift Testing `@Test`.
A manual review.

Method.description: Whether a record comes from a test run or from a reviewer.

oneOf.description: Written by the Rust guard or the Swift trait during a test run.
Written by `cargo xtask evidence new` and filled in by a reviewer.

Problem.description: One problem that fails a run.

message.description: A lowercase sentence naming the rule.

recordId.description: The record it concerns, or null for a run level problem.

ProblemCode.description: The kinds of problem that fail a run.

oneOf.description: A raw record could not be decoded, or breaks a rule.
A record's kind differs from the run's kind.
The same test identity appears twice.
A record is still `NOT_RUN` although the command exited 0.
The fixture credential prefix showed up in the run output.

RunContext.description:
What the wrapper knows about a run, computed once at its start.

`cargo xtask evidence run` writes it to `run.json` and copies it into
every record of `report.json`; `cargo xtask evidence new` fills it for a
manual record. Raw record files written by a test carry none.

baseline.description:
How the host compares with `evidence/baseline-host.json`, or null
while that file does not exist.

command.description: The argv the wrapper ran, or null for a manual record.

host.description: The machine the run happened on.

runId.description: The run ID from the wrapper, or null for a manual record.

runKind.description: The kind of the run, or null for a manual record.

sourceCommit.description: The commit that was tested, from `git rev-parse HEAD`.

sourceDirty.description:
True when `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=normal` was not
empty at the start of the run. A dirty run is never release evidence.

toolchain.description: Toolchain versions found on the host.

Source.description: Where a provider or runtime under test came from.

oneOf.description: A runtime Stackly installs and owns.
A runtime found on the system, such as a Homebrew one.
A fake or fixture. Never used by a native record.

Status.description: The status of a record (PRD section 28).

oneOf.description: No result was observed yet. Every record starts here.
The test or review passed.
The test or review failed.
A prerequisite (binary, hardware, signing) was missing.
Manual only: the scope is outside the baseline.

Subject.description: One provider or runtime a test ran against.

digest.description: The SHA-256 of the artifact as 64 lowercase hex characters, or null.

version.description: The exact version, read from the running binary.

byKind.description: Records per kind, with every kind present.

byStatus.description: Records per status, with every status present.

TestIdentity.description:
The identity of a test: `(language, package, target, name)`, plus where
it lives.

file.description: The source file, relative to the workspace root in `report.json`.

line.description: The line of the guard or the test.

name.description:
Rust: the libtest test path. Swift: the test ID without module and
location. Manual: the title.

target.description: Rust: `CARGO_CRATE_NAME`. Swift: the module name. Manual: null.

Toolchain.description: Toolchain versions found on the host.

rustc.description: The second token of `rustc --version`, for example `1.99.1`.

swift.description:
The version number from `swift --version`, for example `6.4`, or
null without Swift.

xcode.description:
The two lines of `xcodebuild -version` joined, for example
`27.0 (27A266a)`, or null without Xcode.
